text:
sam: Heads-up — Canary v3.7 landed for model-x with the tokenizer tweak and we’re seeing a ~2.5x p99 latency jump on a subset of hosts. Noticed at 09:12 UTC.

maria: wtf. Is this noisy-tenant again or something in the tokenizer change? :thinking_face:

raj: early signals look like KV cache miss rate spiked on those hosts around the same time. I’ll pull profiler.

perf-bot: Deploy canary v3.7 -> 10% traffic (hostpool-a) completed at 09:10 UTC

lee: I’m seeing batch sizes drop from ~8 to ~3 on the victims. Kernel selection logs show more small-kernel paths chosen — `op_small_seq` instead of `op_fused_long`.

jin: tokenizer change was small: collapsed certain unicode sequences into longer token spans. Could shift seq length distribution toward shorter sequences? that seems backwards tho.

raj: pasted profiler dump (top few lines):
```
09:13:01 host=host-17
kernel_calls: op_small_seq 4723 (62%), op_fused_long 1480 (19%), kv_get 13200, kv_miss 4200 (31.8%)
batching: avg_batch=3.2, inflight=5
cpu wait: 14ms, gpu queue latency p99=210ms
```

maria: kv_miss at 31% is huge. Did we change key formation in tokenizer? If subtokens change, prefixes used for KV cache may differ causing misses.

sam: No code in serving touched KV key format. tokenizer produced longer tokens for some emojis and collapsed them, so prefix lengths used by prefetcher could be misaligned.

lee: I instrumented the prefetcher: it was hitting an unexpected codepath where prefetcher lock contention rose — many `prefetch_lock.acquire()` calls queued, causing per-request stall. Stack traces show prefetcher tries to allocate KV fetch futures per token.

raj: log snippet:
```
[09:12:58] prefetcher: token_span=7 -> scheduling 7 kv_fetch futures
[09:12:58] prefetcher: queued fetches 512, active_fetches 128 -> acquire wait
[09:12:58] kernel-decider: fallback to op_small_seq due to low batch viability
```

jin: That explains kernel selection change — batching heuristic sees fewer batched requests (prefetch stalls reduce concurrency) so kernel-decider prefers low-latency small kernels, increasing total overhead.

maria: Could noisy neighbor amplify this? If host had a tenant with lots of tiny requests, prefetcher queue would blow up.

sam: Checked host labels: yes host-17 had a bursty tenant right when canary traffic went to it. But why only canary? The new token spans cause more kv fetches per request so small bursty requests multiplied the pressure.

lee: Root cause hypothesis: tokenizer changed token spans -> increases number of KV lookups per request for some inputs -> prefetcher schedules many futures -> lock contention -> reduced batching -> kernel-decider picks small kernels -> p99 spike.

raj: Quick mitigation options:
- revert tokenizer change for canary
- patch prefetcher to cap futures per-request (e.g., max 4)
- add backpressure in prefetcher queue to avoid acquire-blocking request threads
- make kernel-decider prefer fallback to fused kernels when prefetched kvs pending

maria: Revert canary for now? We need to stop user-visible p99 ASAP.

sam: Rolling back canary to v3.6 on hostpool-a now. ETA ~3m. @perf-bot can you start a perf dashboard snapshot?

perf-bot: Perf snapshot requested: dashboard url https://perf.redwood/shot/2912345678

jin: In parallel I’ll push a quick prefetcher cap in a hotfix branch; patch is tiny. If rollback fixes it we still should land cap as defense.

lee: I’ll add logging to measure kv_lookups_per_request and prefetch_queue_lengths across hosts.

raj: After rollback completes we should run a targeted canary with synthetic workloads that exercise emoji-heavy inputs and measure kv_miss and batch sizes.

sam: Update: rollback completed at 09:16 UTC. Early numbers: host-17 p99 back to baseline, avg_batch=7.8, kv_miss=5.1%.

maria: nice. Leave canary off until we have prefetch cap + metrics. Create a short postmortem and action items.

jin: PR for prefetch cap: link https://git.redwood/infra/prefetcher/pull/412 — adds per-request cap and queue backpressure. Will run internal canary.

lee: Added kv-lookup and prefetch-queue panels to runtime-dashboard. Link https://grafana/redwood/runtime/prefetch

sam: OK team, next steps: (1) ship prefetch cap hotfix to canary, (2) run synthetic tokenizer stress, (3) evaluate kernel-decider fallback tuning, (4) update rollout checklist to include kv_miss guardrails. I’ll create tasks.

maria: +1. add a note: any tokenizer change must include sim on KV profile to catch this early.

raj: filing incident summary and assigning follow-ups.

perf-bot: Incident logged: INC-2026-0143 | assigned: raj, jin, lee | severity: P2
